# Fork CI and publication

CI uses Node 22 and Corepack's `packageManager` pin (pnpm 10.29.2).
The three workspace packages build in dependency order. Lint is a separate,
required step. ESLint 9 uses the repository's existing legacy configuration.
Core (with coverage), source and cells tests run without watch mode.
React 18 and 19 each get an isolated install, followed by an explicit version
overlay and core tests. Only these disposable compatibility jobs modify their
lockfile. The committed pnpm lockfile is never regenerated by normal CI.

`test-projects` retains the standalone Next/CRA fixtures and their existing
`npm ci` lockfiles; these are outside the pnpm workspace. Its existing bootstrap
installs dependencies and links the local core package; it does not build the
fixture applications. Coveralls upload has been removed; core coverage remains
in the test output and the core-coverage Actions artifact.

## Publication (never run as part of verification)

Release CI and Beta CI are manual workflows, dispatched from main with an
existing version tag. Tag pushes do not publish. Tags must resolve to a commit
on main, match all three package versions, and have the correct release channel:
`vX.Y.Z` for `latest`, `vX.Y.Z-prerelease` for `beta`. The tagged commit must
include this workflow and its validation script. Current alpha versions can
only pass the beta workflow's validation.

The job checks package names, restricted access and GitHub Packages registry
before installation/build/lint/tests. It publishes core, cells and source via
pnpm so workspace aliases are rewritten for consumers. The workflow is limited
to jlhartley/glide-data-grid. Authentication uses GITHUB_TOKEN only on the
publication step, with contents:read and packages:write; checkout credentials
are not persisted. No NPM_TOKEN or npmjs publication action is used.

Existing packages must grant this repository Actions write access in their
GitHub Packages settings. Package visibility is managed there; this workflow
does not change it. Publication is not atomic: if a registry error interrupts
publication, inspect which versions already exist before retrying.

## Local verification (no publication)

```sh
corepack enable
pnpm --version # must be 10.29.2
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm run build
ESLINT_USE_FLAT_CONFIG=false pnpm run lint
pnpm run test --run --coverage
pnpm run test-source --run
pnpm run test-cells --run
pnpm run test-projects
```

In separate disposable checkouts, repeat the locked install and run
`pnpm run test-18` or `pnpm run test-19`. These commands intentionally replace
the React dependencies and update that checkout's manifest and lockfile.

## Validation on 27 October 2026

Local runtime: Node 24.22.1 (workflow runtime: Node 22), Corepack 0.34.6,
pnpm 10.29.2. Frozen installation and all three workspace builds passed.
YAML parsing, Bash syntax, JavaScript syntax and whitespace checks passed.
Release validation accepted a matching beta tag and rejected a stable-channel
mismatch, branch name, nonexistent tag and npmjs registry in a temporary Git
fixture. Nothing was published.

The current lint configuration fails loading SonarJS's recommended config
(`Unexpected top-level property "name"`). The existing test/lockfile setup also
has failures: core 223 failed / 164 passed; source 5 failed / 2 passed; cells
4 failed / 58 passed. Invalid React hook calls feature in all suites; the locked
workspace peer auto-installs use React 19.2.4 while the runner uses 19.2.0.
These failures are left visible, rather than weakening lint rules or test
assertions. CI attempts all three suites after a successful build even when
lint or another suite fails. A failed check blocks publication.

React 18/19 dependency overlays and the legacy consumer bootstrap were not
executed locally. Their commands above remain available for disposable
checkouts and GitHub Actions verification.
